name: DadsFam Live Chat
author: dadsfam

sections.description:
DadsFam Live Chat puts a modern chat window on your site, gives your team a proper Inbox to answer from, and adds a help centre — with an AI assistant built in that looks after visitors whenever nobody is around.

Everything runs on your own WordPress site. There is no account to create, no cloud service, no API key and no monthly fee. Conversations are stored only in your own database, and nothing is sent to an outside service.

The built-in AI assistant

The assistant runs entirely inside your WordPress, on your own server. It does not use OpenAI, ChatGPT, Claude or any other outside service, there is no API key, and nothing about your visitors or their conversations leaves your site. It costs nothing to run.

  • It reads your site. Pages, posts, products and help articles — you choose which. It keeps up by itself whenever you save a change.
  • It understands questions however they are typed. Spelling mistakes are corrected against the words your own site uses, words are matched by their roots (“delivered”, “delivery”, “deliveries”; “bit” and “bitten”), and it knows everyday words that mean the same thing (courier and delivery, kids and children, Amex and American Express). Chat spelling and South African English are fine too: “hoe much 4 a big dog per nite”, “can I fetch my dogs on Sunday?”.
  • It works things out instead of just matching words. “If I cancel 10 days before, do I get my money back?” finds your rule for 7 to 14 days. “We’ll only get there at 11pm” finds what you say about arriving after 20:00. “My clutch is slipping. How long will you need the car?” finds the clutch row of a long price table and answers with just that row. “What’s your cheapest room?” compares the prices in your table.
  • It answers with the exact sentences that matter, not a whole page, and adds a link to read more. Ask two things at once (“What time is check-in? Is breakfast included?”) and it answers both.
  • It never guesses. When it is not sure, it says so, offers a person, or takes the visitor’s email for your team. You choose how sure it must be.
  • WooCommerce aware. It answers “do you have…” and “anything under R500?” with product cards showing live prices and stock, finds the exact option asked for (“48 rolls, 350 sheets”) with an Add to cart button, and answers “any specials?” from your live sale prices. Signed-in customers see their own orders; anyone else checks an order safely, as the order number and the email address it was placed with must both match. Sign-in, password and guest-checkout questions are answered from your WooCommerce settings.
  • It knows the basics — your opening hours (including “are you open on Saturday?”), phone, email and address, even if they are only written on your pages — and hands over to a person whenever a visitor asks, or seems unhappy.
  • It learns. Questions it could not answer are collected for you to answer once. Answers your team gives in chats are picked up for your approval (or straight away once two chats get the same answer). Visitors’ 👍 and 👎 push good answers up and poor ones down, and it works out new word links by itself from what visitors found helpful.
  • It shows its working. The AI Assistant screen has a test chat that shows how it understood a question, what it found and how sure it was.

How it works, for the curious: questions are broken into word roots, corrected, and expanded with related words; every passage of your site is ranked the way search engines rank pages, with extra weight where the words asked appear together and where amounts, times and dates fit; and the best-matching sentences are picked out to form the answer. It is not a large language model, so it cannot make things up — every answer comes from your own site or from what you taught it.

You decide when it talks: only when your team is away (the default), first on every chat with people on request, or never — just suggesting replies to your team.

Live chat your visitors will like

  • A clean chat window that matches your brand colour, in light or dark, on desktop and phone.
  • Home, Messages and Help tabs: a greeting, who is online, instant answers from your help articles and the conversation itself.
  • Quick-reply buttons, “Seen” receipts, typing indicators, emoji, ratings, transcripts by email and a leave-a-message form when nobody is around.
  • Chats carry on across pages and tabs, and survive a dropped connection.
  • It costs nothing until it is used: the chat bubble loads without a single request to your server.
  • Draws itself in its own sealed-off area, so your theme’s styles cannot break it — and it cannot break your theme.

An Inbox your team will actually enjoy

  • Waiting, My chats, All live chats, With your AI, Messages and History.
  • Reply suggestions from your saved answers, your site and your saved replies, right above the reply box.
  • Type / for saved replies. Private notes inside the conversation. Transfers, tags and keyboard shortcuts.
  • The visitor’s details beside the chat: the page they are on, the pages they visited, their device, their earlier chats and their WooCommerce orders.
  • Take over from the AI assistant at any time, and teach it with one click from any reply you send.
  • Sound and desktop alerts, dark mode, and it works properly on a phone.
  • A “Chat Agent” role for staff who should answer chats without being able to edit your site.

A help centre

  • A help centre at an address you choose (yourdomain.com/help/ by default): a search box that answers as people type, your topics, the most helpful articles and every article, laid out to suit your theme.
  • Put the same help centre on any page with the “Help Centre” block or the [dadsfam_help_center] shortcode.
  • “Was this helpful?” on every article, related articles, and the same articles inside the chat window.
  • A “Chat Button” block and [dadsfam_chat_button] shortcode. Any link to #chat opens the chat too.

It looks after itself

  • An hourly check repairs missing database tables, sets forgotten “online” team members to away, tidies stuck chats and keeps the assistant’s knowledge fresh.
  • If a security plugin or your host blocks the WordPress REST API, the chat switches to a backup connection by itself.
  • The Health screen checks everything in plain English and fixes most problems with one click.

Safe and private

  • Bots are stopped with signed tickets, a hidden trap field and rate limits. Blocklists understand IP ranges (IPv4 and IPv6), email domains and words, and throwaway email addresses can be refused.
  • Visitors’ IP addresses cannot be faked to get around a block, and you can shorten or not store IP addresses at all.
  • Finished chats can be deleted automatically after the number of days you choose.
  • Works with WordPress’s own Export and Erase Personal Data tools and suggests privacy-policy wording.
  • Works alongside DadsFam AntiSpam when it is installed, so its blocklists and checks apply to chats too.

For developers

  • AI tools connected to WordPress through the Abilities API (WordPress 6.9 and later) can read and answer chats, check health and teach the assistant.
  • Open the chat from your own code with DadsFamLiveChat.open().
  • Filter where the widget shows with dadsfam_live_chat_show_widget.

A word about PRO

Right, let me be straight with you, because I hate being sold to as much as you do.

There is no PRO version of Live Chat. Everything above is free and it stays free. The AI assistant, the Inbox, the help centre, the WooCommerce product answers and order checks, saved replies, transcripts and the rest are not premium features, and if I put them behind a paywall I would be taking the mickey. No trial, no locked buttons, no “upgrade to unlock” anywhere.

I am a dad in Cape Town, and I built this because my own shops needed a chat that did not cost a fortune every month or send my customers’ conversations to somebody else’s server. That is the honest reason. Not “unlock your potential”, not “supercharge your workflow”.

So if it does everything you need, brilliant. Genuinely. Use it, and I hope it saves you a few late-night messages. The rest of what I build is at plugins.dadsfam.co.za.

Either way, thanks for using something I built. — Zak, DadsFam

External services

This plugin does not connect to any service of its own. It has no home-phoning, no analytics and no licence checks. The AI assistant, the chat and the help centre all run on your own WordPress site, and conversations are stored only in your own database.

Two things are worth knowing:

  • The Health screen checks that chat can connect by making one request from your site to its own REST API address (a “loopback” request). It is sent to your own domain and nothing is sent anywhere else.
  • Team members’ pictures in the Inbox come from WordPress’s own avatar setting, which uses Gravatar by default. You can change or switch this off under Settings → Discussion. The plugin itself sends nothing to Gravatar.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “DadsFam Live Chat”, then Install and Activate. (Or upload the ZIP under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.)
  2. Click Set it all up for me — on the Plugins screen right after activating, or at the top of Live Chat → Dashboard. One click switches the chat and the AI assistant on with the best settings, finds your contact details on your own pages and has the assistant read your whole site.
  3. Open the Inbox and switch yourself Online to take chats.
  4. Under Live Chat → AI Assistant, try the assistant out and tell it anything your site doesn’t say.
  5. Make it yours under Live Chat → Settings — brand colour, greeting, opening hours and email alerts.
sections.faq:
Does the AI assistant send my data to OpenAI, ChatGPT or anyone else?

No. The assistant runs inside your own WordPress. It reads your own pages, products and help articles, understands questions with a language engine built into the plugin, and does all its work on your own server. There is no outside AI service, no API key and no fee.

How do I switch the AI assistant off?

Untick “Switch the AI assistant on” under Live Chat → AI Assistant. To keep it off whatever the settings say, add define( 'DADSFAM_LIVE_CHAT_AI_OFF', true ); to wp-config.php. Live chat, the Inbox and the help centre carry on exactly as before.

Is it a real AI?

It is a language-understanding and search engine built for one job: answering questions from your own content. It corrects spelling, understands word forms and related words, ranks every passage of your site and picks out the sentences that answer the question — and it learns from your team and your visitors. It is not a large language model, which is exactly why it never invents answers.

What does it do when it doesn’t know?

It says so honestly. If someone from your team is online it offers to bring them in; if not, it takes the visitor’s email so you can reply, and adds the question to Knowledge → To teach so you can answer it once for good.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. With WooCommerce active the assistant also answers product questions with live prices and stock, and checks order status, and the Inbox shows each visitor’s orders.

Will it slow my site down?

No. The chat script loads after your page has finished, and the bubble is drawn without asking your server anything. The server is only contacted once a visitor opens the chat or already has a conversation going.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. The chat talks to your site through its own connection that tells every page cache, CDN and browser never to cache it. If you change the chat’s settings and do not see the change, clear your page cache once.

My security plugin blocks the REST API. Will chat still work?

Yes. If the REST API is blocked, the chat and the Inbox switch to a backup connection by themselves, and Health tells you it happened.

Who can answer chats?

Administrators, Editors and Shop Managers by default, plus anyone you give the “Chat Agent” role. Choose which roles under Settings → Availability.

Can I change how the help centre looks?

Yes. With a block theme, the help centre and its articles are templates you can edit like any other in Appearance → Editor → Templates (“Help centre” and “Help article”). With a classic theme, the help centre uses your theme’s header and footer; add an archive-dadsfam_help.php template to your theme if you want to replace it. The help centre’s colour follows the chat’s brand colour.

Can I put a chat button on a page?

Yes. Use the “Chat Button” block, the [dadsfam_chat_button text="Chat with us"] shortcode, or link any text or button to #chat.

What happens to my chats from version 2?

They move across automatically when you update, along with your settings and saved replies. Version 2’s leftover files are removed, and the old tables are only removed once every conversation is confirmed as moved.

Email alerts are not arriving.

Open Live Chat → Health and press “Send a test”. If the test never arrives, your server cannot send email reliably — an SMTP plugin fixes that.

What happens if I delete the plugin?

Your chats, settings, help articles and everything the assistant learned are kept, in case you reinstall — unless you switch on “Delete everything when the plugin is deleted” under Settings → Privacy & data.
sections.changelog:
3.4.0

One-click Quick setup, and a sharper AI assistant.

  • New: Quick setup. One button on the Dashboard (and on the Plugins screen right after you activate) switches the chat and the AI assistant on with the best settings for your site, finds your email address, phone number and address on your own pages, and has the assistant read every page, post and product. It only fills in what is empty and tells you exactly what it did. The Settings and AI Assistant screens have a “Not sure what to pick?” shortcut to it.
  • New: “Where are you, and can I get there by tram?”, “how far from the station?”, “is there parking?” get your address and how to get there, in your site’s own words.
  • New: product questions are answered from the product’s own details: “does it come with gas?”, “I’m 185 cm, which length do I need?”, “how heavy is it?”, “does the tent come with a footprint?”. When neither the product nor the rest of the site says (“is the down RDS certified?”, “do the cars have heated seats?”), the assistant says it doesn’t know instead of showing something unrelated.
  • New: “What’s the cheapest car?” or “your most expensive room?” finds the right row of a price list on your pages, not only among WooCommerce products. “What sleeping bag for snow camping?” shows the bag made for snow, not every bag.
  • Improved: “not” questions. “What isn’t covered?” gets the whole list; “is a flat tyre covered?” says which list the answer comes from (“From ‘What is never covered'”); “what cards can’t I use?” and “what payment methods don’t you take?” quote your own words; “who can’t rent a car?” gets the age and licence rules.
  • Improved: holidays. “Are you open on Cup Day?” answers for that day, “your hours on St Patrick’s Day?” gives the hours with it, and “if I order on Cup Day, when will it be sent?” uses your own line about that day.
  • Improved: follow-ups. “What about Perth?” after a shipping question gives the rates for Perth (big towns and cities are matched to their state or province in South Africa, Australia, New Zealand, the USA and Canada), and “and for a week?” stays with the price list it follows.
  • Improved: “What is [your business]?” says what the business is, and how it began, rather than only its history; its short name (“Atalia” for “Atalia Car & Van Hire”) is recognised. “Are you hiring?” is never answered with “we don’t hire out tents”.
  • Improved: “can I return it if I’ve opened it?”, “what if I’m sick on the day?”, “if I buy it today, can it be returned after Christmas?” and long questions that name a place (“my mom in Paarl…”) find the right rule.
  • Improved: delivery-time answers leave out what to do with a damaged parcel, a long list is never cut off in the middle of a word, and a single list item reads as a sentence.

3.3.0

The AI assistant knows the business it works for, explains how ordering works, reads “not”, “except” and “what if…” questions properly, and knows when to pass a question on instead of guessing.

  • New: “What is [your business]?”, “tell me about you guys”, “who are you guys?”, “what do you do?”, “who owns it?”, “how long have you been around?” and “are you legit?” are answered from your About and front pages (or your tagline), with what you sell. When the site doesn’t say, the assistant says so honestly.
  • New: “How does ordering work?”, “how do I order?” and “can I order by phone or WhatsApp?” get the steps in your site’s own words, or plain steps, plus what your shop’s settings add: guest checkout or an account, the ways to pay, delivery or collection and any free-delivery amount.
  • New: questions with “not” or “except” (“what isn’t covered?”, “which items can’t be returned?”, “what payment methods don’t you take?”) get the exclusions, not the list of what is included. “How much do I pay?” is no longer answered from a “what we don’t pay for” section.
  • New: “what if” questions (“can I return it if I don’t like it?”, “what if it doesn’t fit?”, “what if I’m not home?”) are answered by the rule for that case, such as the change-of-mind section.
  • New: help that needs the team (cancelling an order, a double charge, a confirmation or password email that never came, a refund, becoming a supplier) gets the next step and how to reach the team, not a random page.
  • New: “What’s your best seller?”, “what’s the cheapest?”, “I’m on a tight budget” and “what would you recommend?” give the right products (the cheapest is now worked out properly for products with options). Questions that name no product get a friendly “what are you shopping for?”.
  • New: delivery times (“how long does delivery take?”, “can I get it by Friday?”), payment safety, instalments and lay-by (honestly, from your checkout settings), proof of payment and a bank-transfer reference, and holiday hours (“I don’t have special holiday hours”) are answered properly.
  • Improved: follow-ups. “And how long?”, “what about EFT?”, “where from?” and “how much is it?” are read with the question before them.
  • Improved: the assistant passes a question on instead of guessing. Questions about returns, warranty, delivery, payment, cancelling, reviews or social media are only answered from a passage that talks about that topic, and never from a blog or news post that just uses the same word. Off-topic questions such as the weather get a polite “I can only help with this site”.
  • Improved: a timetable or price list for each branch gives every branch’s lines, a list gets the line that introduces it, a question’s own case is answered whole, and an FAQ question run together with its answer on the page is read as two lines.
  • Improved: more everyday chat is understood: “anyone there?”, “cheers mate”, “grand, cheers”, “need help”, “hw do i ordr”, “wheres my parcl”, “how 2 pay”, “shut” for “close”, “this arvo”, “Paddy’s Day” and “Cup Day”.
  • Improved: the assistant re-reads your site once after this update, in the background.

3.2.0

The AI assistant keeps helping after it hands a chat to the team, understands everyday chat (“ok”, “hello?”, “sorry, I meant…”), and walks customers from product to checkout.

  • Fixed: after handing a chat to the team, the assistant went quiet until someone joined. It now keeps answering while the visitor waits in the queue or has left a message, says when something has gone to the team, and never pages the team twice or offers “talk to a person” again.
  • New: “Hello?”, “are you still there?” and “???” get “I’m still here”, with where the chat stands: next in line, or the team will reply to their email.
  • New: “OK”, “cool”, “got it”, “done” and “no” are understood as replies and never searched. “Yes” to an offer (“Want to see the 18 products on special?”) does what was offered. After a product is shown, “done” means it is in the cart, and the assistant points to the cart and checkout.
  • New: corrections. “Sorry, I meant the anti-spam one”, “I meant Pretoria” and “*lavender” put the last question right instead of starting over.
  • New: the buying journey, end to end. “Order the backups plugin please”, “I want to do a test order as a guest”, “I added it to my cart”, “how do I check out?”, “I’ve placed my order” and “I paid” each get the right next step: the product ready for the cart, Cart and Checkout buttons, the ways to pay, whether guests can check out, and how to follow the order.
  • New: “What do you sell?” lists your shop’s main categories. “Which plugins do you offer?” or “What are your best treatments?” gets the whole list from your pages, not one item.
  • New: “Which coffees have you got?” lists the products in your category of that name, and “what services do you offer?” lists the sections of the page about them. A business with two branches gets both addresses for “where are you?”.
  • New: “What are your bank details?” gives the account set up for bank transfers at checkout. “Can you post to the USA?” is answered from the countries you sell to, and “Ireland” is no longer taken for “Northern Ireland”.
  • Improved: one word or two. “antispam”, “anti spam” and “Anti-Spam” find the same thing (product options too), as do “web site” and “website”, “gift voucher” and “gift card”. A stray word from a phone’s autocorrect no longer hides the product the rest of the message names.
  • Improved: everyday words from other English-speaking countries (“cuppa”, “arvo”, “togs”, “quid”, “kia ora”, “sweet as”, “chur”), shortened words (“physio”, “hydro”), typos in short words (“cofee”) and “café”-style accents are understood. “How much caffeine is in it?” is read as a question about the product, not its price, and “a present for my mum, about 25 quid” finds gifts within budget.
  • Improved: page buttons and labels (“⬇ Download”, “Read more”, “Version 1.4.0”, “← Back to…”) and “for the full list, see…” lines are no longer read out as answers. A product page is no longer given as the answer to a question that is not about it (“what’s the weather tomorrow?”), and “can you fix my car?” is not answered with a car-wash product.
  • Improved: the assistant re-reads your site once after this update, in the background.

3.1.0

The AI assistant now handles real shop conversations from your own WooCommerce data, and visitors can end their chat again.

  • Fixed: visitors can end their own chat again. “End chat” now asks “End this chat?” and closes it; it used to close the menu instead.
  • New: signed-in customers can ask “order history”, “where is my order?” or “what did I order?” and see their own orders as cards (status, items, total) with a My orders button. No order number or email needed. Guests get a Sign in button, or can give their order number and email as before.
  • New: when a visitor signs in during a chat, the assistant knows on their next message, and “I am signed in” is understood. A chat that belongs to one account is never shown to anyone else on the same browser.
  • New: the assistant picks the exact product option a visitor describes (“48 rolls, 350 sheets”) with its own price, and product cards have an Add to cart button that puts that exact option in the cart.
  • New: “Can you place an order for me?”, “How do I order?” and “Can I order on WhatsApp?” get a proper answer: the product ready for the cart, or how ordering works in your shop’s own words, the ways to pay and whether guests can check out.
  • New: specials. “Any specials on toilet paper?” is answered from your live sale prices and sale dates: what is on special, honestly what is not, and the deals and combos that include it.
  • New: account questions (signing in, a forgotten password, creating an account, “do I need an account?”, changing an address) are answered from your WooCommerce settings, with buttons to the right page.
  • New: “How do I pay?” and “Do you take card?” are answered from the ways your checkout actually takes payment (and from your own pages when they say more). “Can you deliver to Namibia?”, “Do you deliver on a Saturday?” and “Can I collect my order?” are answered from your shipping settings and pages: the countries you ship to, your delivery days and your collection points (by area; street addresses stay at checkout).
  • New: “My order arrived and a bottle was cracked” gets your own words on damaged or lost parcels and a person to help. Bulk and quote requests get your bulk-order wording and an offer of a quote. Signed-in customers can say “reorder the toilet paper I bought last time” and get that exact option ready for the cart.
  • New: follow-ups such as “how much is the bigger one?”, “what scents do you have?” and “what’s the difference between Combo 1 and Combo 2?” are understood. A question about something the shop doesn’t sell (“gift vouchers?”, “petrol prices”) gets an honest answer instead of unrelated products.
  • New: “How much did I pay for the router?”, “what’s the total of my order that’s still processing?”, “what did I order two weeks ago?” and “how many orders have I placed?” are answered for a signed-in customer from their own orders, including the option they bought (“48 rolls, 350 sheets”).
  • New: “Do you deliver to Johannesburg?”, “What delivery options do I have?” and “How much is delivery to Durban?” list your checkout’s delivery methods and costs for the visitor’s area, from your shipping zones (“I stay in Pretoria” is remembered). “Is it free to collect from Brooklyn?” is answered from your collection points.
  • New: “Is House Combo 3 on special? How much do I save?” gives the price now, the usual price and the saving. “What’s in the kitchen combo?” lists what comes in it.
  • New: “What reference must I use for EFT?” and “I paid by EFT, when will you send my order?” are answered from your payment method’s own instructions, and “Can I pay with EFT?” names the way to choose at checkout.
  • New: “Tracking says delivered but nothing came”, “my parcel never arrived”, “I ordered rose but you sent peach”, “there was no hand soap in the box”, “it’s too small, can I swap it?” and “I wore it once, can I send it back?” get your own words on lost parcels, returns and exchanges, and a person to help. “How do I delete my account?” quotes your privacy policy’s contact for deletion requests.
  • New: “Am I chatting to a bot?” gets an honest answer, with a person on offer. Everyday shop questions in Afrikaans are understood (“hoeveel kos die bleach?”), and British and American spellings (“licence”, “license”) find each other.
  • New: small talk such as “tell me a joke”, “who are you?” or “what can you do?” gets a friendly answer instead of a search result.
  • Improved: better judgement about what counts as an answer. A blog post that only shares a word with a question (an “order history” question and a news article that says “ordered”) is no longer given as the answer. Delivery, payment, account and order questions are answered from the shop’s own pages and facts first. “What is…?” questions get the line that explains it, and “How much…?” gets the line with the amount.
  • Improved: an answer you taught is used only for the question you taught it for and close rewordings, and “please sign in first” is never said to someone who is signed in. Replies such as “let me check” or “please sign in first” are no longer learned from chats.
  • Improved: questions about now (“petrol price at the moment”, “weather tomorrow”, “who won on Saturday”) are answered from your newest post with its date, or not at all when the newest post is too old to still be true. “Do you sell…?” and “Do you repair…?” are answered from your shop and pages, not from a news post.
  • Improved: products with options count as in stock when any option is in stock, products with up to 12 options list them all, and a product’s tags, category and SKU are never read out as an answer.
  • Improved: long pages (a privacy policy that also holds your shipping and returns terms, say) are read to the end, and an FAQ question is never split from its answer. Typos in product names and options (“speek easy cofee”, “frankinsence”) still find them. “Are you hiring?”, “Do you do gift wrapping?”, “is it gluten free?” and “do you price match?” get an honest “I don’t know” with a person on offer, not an unrelated post or product.
  • Improved: a follow-up about the product just shown (“do I have to renew it every year?”) is answered from its description; “where can I get it again?” gets the line that says where, “how do I fix it?” the line that says what fixes it, “who made it?” the line that names them, and a question about a brand is answered from what your site says about that brand. Answers you taught are found despite typos, and “place an order for me” uses your taught answer whichever product is named.
  • Improved: scripts and styles inside page content are no longer read as text. The assistant re-reads your site once after this update.
  • Improved: product names in the chat leave off the shop name at the end (“Toilet Paper | DadsFam” shows as “Toilet Paper”), products with options show “From R…”, and specials show the old price crossed out.

3.0.0

A complete rebuild.

  • New: a built-in AI assistant that runs on your own server — no ChatGPT, no outside service, no fees. It reads your pages, products and help articles, understands questions however they are typed (spelling mistakes too), and answers with the exact sentences that matter, with a link to read more.
  • New: the assistant answers product questions with live prices and stock, checks order status safely (order number and email must match), knows your opening hours and contact details, and hands over to a person when asked or when it is not sure. It never guesses.
  • New: the assistant works things out rather than just matching words — amounts, times and dates in a question are checked against the rules on your pages (“10 days before” finds your “7 to 14 days” rule, “8 months ago” is inside a 12-month warranty, “9pm” is after hours), the row of a table a question names is found even in a long price list, a message that tells a story before it asks is read for its question, prices in your tables are compared for “cheapest” questions, and two questions in one message each get an answer.
  • New: the assistant learns by itself. Questions it could not answer are collected for you to answer once; answers your team gives in chats are learned (after your OK, or straight away when the team gives the same answer twice); and visitors’ 👍/👎 push good answers up and poor ones down.
  • New: a brand-new Inbox with Waiting, My chats, All live chats, With your AI, Messages and History; reply suggestions; private notes inside the conversation; the visitor’s pages, earlier chats and WooCommerce orders beside the chat; transfers, tags, keyboard shortcuts, dark mode, sound and desktop alerts. It works properly on phones.
  • New: a new chat window for visitors with Home, Messages and Help tabs, help articles inside the chat, instant answers as they search, quick-reply buttons, “Seen” receipts, ratings, transcripts and a leave-a-message form. Your theme’s styles can no longer break it, and it no longer slows pages down.
  • New: a help centre — its own page at /help/ with instant answers as people type, help articles with topics, the same help centre on any page (block or shortcode), “Was this helpful?” votes and related articles.
  • New: Dashboard, AI Assistant, Knowledge, Settings (with a live preview), Health and Help & Support screens, all in plain English.
  • New: opening hours, going “away” automatically when you close the Inbox, a polite busy message, a “Chat Agent” role for staff, and a choice of which roles can answer chats.
  • New: it looks after itself — an hourly check repairs missing tables, sets forgotten “online” people to away, tidies stuck chats and keeps the assistant’s knowledge fresh. If a security plugin blocks the chat’s connection, a backup connection takes over by itself.
  • New: AI assistants you connect to WordPress (through the Abilities API in WordPress 6.9 and later) can read and answer chats, run health checks and teach the built-in assistant.
  • Improved: safer — visitors’ secret chat keys are stored scrambled, bots are stopped with signed tickets, IP addresses cannot be faked to dodge a block, and blocklists understand IPv6 ranges.
  • Improved: privacy — works with WordPress’s Export and Erase Personal Data tools, can shorten or skip IP addresses, deletes old chats automatically and suggests privacy-policy wording.
  • Changed: the separate fast endpoint (chat-fast.php) is gone; chat now uses WordPress’s own REST API with a built-in backup route.
  • Updating: your chats, settings and saved replies from version 2 move across automatically, and the old files are cleaned up.

2.0.4

  • Mobile polish: the iPhone keyboard no longer hides the message box, pop-ups no longer stack on top of each other, and buttons no longer stay highlighted after a tap.

2.0.3

  • Fixed: the History button now works on phones.

2.0.2

2.0.1

short_description: Free live chat and help centre with a built-in AI assistant that runs on your own server, answers from your site and learns from your team.
description:
DadsFam Live Chat puts a modern chat window on your site, gives your team a proper Inbox to answer from, and adds a help centre — with an AI assistant built in that looks after visitors whenever nobody is around.

Everything runs on your own WordPress site. There is no account to create, no cloud service, no API key and no monthly fee. Conversations are stored only in your own database, and nothing is sent to an outside service.

The built-in AI assistant

The assistant runs entirely inside your WordPress, on your own server. It does not use OpenAI, ChatGPT, Claude or any other outside service, there is no API key, and nothing about your visitors or their conversations leaves your site. It costs nothing to run.

  • It reads your site. Pages, posts, products and help articles — you choose which. It keeps up by itself whenever you save a change.
  • It understands questions however they are typed. Spelling mistakes are corrected against the words your own site uses, words are matched by their roots (“delivered”, “delivery”, “deliveries”; “bit” and “bitten”), and it knows everyday words that mean the same thing (courier and delivery, kids and children, Amex and American Express). Chat spelling and South African English are fine too: “hoe much 4 a big dog per nite”, “can I fetch my dogs on Sunday?”.
  • It works things out instead of just matching words. “If I cancel 10 days before, do I get my money back?” finds your rule for 7 to 14 days. “We’ll only get there at 11pm” finds what you say about arriving after 20:00. “My clutch is slipping. How long will you need the car?” finds the clutch row of a long price table and answers with just that row. “What’s your cheapest room?” compares the prices in your table.
  • It answers with the exact sentences that matter, not a whole page, and adds a link to read more. Ask two things at once (“What time is check-in? Is breakfast included?”) and it answers both.
  • It never guesses. When it is not sure, it says so, offers a person, or takes the visitor’s email for your team. You choose how sure it must be.
  • WooCommerce aware. It answers “do you have…” and “anything under R500?” with product cards showing live prices and stock, finds the exact option asked for (“48 rolls, 350 sheets”) with an Add to cart button, and answers “any specials?” from your live sale prices. Signed-in customers see their own orders; anyone else checks an order safely, as the order number and the email address it was placed with must both match. Sign-in, password and guest-checkout questions are answered from your WooCommerce settings.
  • It knows the basics — your opening hours (including “are you open on Saturday?”), phone, email and address, even if they are only written on your pages — and hands over to a person whenever a visitor asks, or seems unhappy.
  • It learns. Questions it could not answer are collected for you to answer once. Answers your team gives in chats are picked up for your approval (or straight away once two chats get the same answer). Visitors’ 👍 and 👎 push good answers up and poor ones down, and it works out new word links by itself from what visitors found helpful.
  • It shows its working. The AI Assistant screen has a test chat that shows how it understood a question, what it found and how sure it was.

How it works, for the curious: questions are broken into word roots, corrected, and expanded with related words; every passage of your site is ranked the way search engines rank pages, with extra weight where the words asked appear together and where amounts, times and dates fit; and the best-matching sentences are picked out to form the answer. It is not a large language model, so it cannot make things up — every answer comes from your own site or from what you taught it.

You decide when it talks: only when your team is away (the default), first on every chat with people on request, or never — just suggesting replies to your team.

Live chat your visitors will like

  • A clean chat window that matches your brand colour, in light or dark, on desktop and phone.
  • Home, Messages and Help tabs: a greeting, who is online, instant answers from your help articles and the conversation itself.
  • Quick-reply buttons, “Seen” receipts, typing indicators, emoji, ratings, transcripts by email and a leave-a-message form when nobody is around.
  • Chats carry on across pages and tabs, and survive a dropped connection.
  • It costs nothing until it is used: the chat bubble loads without a single request to your server.
  • Draws itself in its own sealed-off area, so your theme’s styles cannot break it — and it cannot break your theme.

An Inbox your team will actually enjoy

  • Waiting, My chats, All live chats, With your AI, Messages and History.
  • Reply suggestions from your saved answers, your site and your saved replies, right above the reply box.
  • Type / for saved replies. Private notes inside the conversation. Transfers, tags and keyboard shortcuts.
  • The visitor’s details beside the chat: the page they are on, the pages they visited, their device, their earlier chats and their WooCommerce orders.
  • Take over from the AI assistant at any time, and teach it with one click from any reply you send.
  • Sound and desktop alerts, dark mode, and it works properly on a phone.
  • A “Chat Agent” role for staff who should answer chats without being able to edit your site.

A help centre

  • A help centre at an address you choose (yourdomain.com/help/ by default): a search box that answers as people type, your topics, the most helpful articles and every article, laid out to suit your theme.
  • Put the same help centre on any page with the “Help Centre” block or the [dadsfam_help_center] shortcode.
  • “Was this helpful?” on every article, related articles, and the same articles inside the chat window.
  • A “Chat Button” block and [dadsfam_chat_button] shortcode. Any link to #chat opens the chat too.

It looks after itself

  • An hourly check repairs missing database tables, sets forgotten “online” team members to away, tidies stuck chats and keeps the assistant’s knowledge fresh.
  • If a security plugin or your host blocks the WordPress REST API, the chat switches to a backup connection by itself.
  • The Health screen checks everything in plain English and fixes most problems with one click.

Safe and private

  • Bots are stopped with signed tickets, a hidden trap field and rate limits. Blocklists understand IP ranges (IPv4 and IPv6), email domains and words, and throwaway email addresses can be refused.
  • Visitors’ IP addresses cannot be faked to get around a block, and you can shorten or not store IP addresses at all.
  • Finished chats can be deleted automatically after the number of days you choose.
  • Works with WordPress’s own Export and Erase Personal Data tools and suggests privacy-policy wording.
  • Works alongside DadsFam AntiSpam when it is installed, so its blocklists and checks apply to chats too.

For developers

  • AI tools connected to WordPress through the Abilities API (WordPress 6.9 and later) can read and answer chats, check health and teach the assistant.
  • Open the chat from your own code with DadsFamLiveChat.open().
  • Filter where the widget shows with dadsfam_live_chat_show_widget.

A word about PRO

Right, let me be straight with you, because I hate being sold to as much as you do.

There is no PRO version of Live Chat. Everything above is free and it stays free. The AI assistant, the Inbox, the help centre, the WooCommerce product answers and order checks, saved replies, transcripts and the rest are not premium features, and if I put them behind a paywall I would be taking the mickey. No trial, no locked buttons, no “upgrade to unlock” anywhere.

I am a dad in Cape Town, and I built this because my own shops needed a chat that did not cost a fortune every month or send my customers’ conversations to somebody else’s server. That is the honest reason. Not “unlock your potential”, not “supercharge your workflow”.

So if it does everything you need, brilliant. Genuinely. Use it, and I hope it saves you a few late-night messages. The rest of what I build is at plugins.dadsfam.co.za.

Either way, thanks for using something I built. — Zak, DadsFam

External services

This plugin does not connect to any service of its own. It has no home-phoning, no analytics and no licence checks. The AI assistant, the chat and the help centre all run on your own WordPress site, and conversations are stored only in your own database.

Two things are worth knowing:

  • The Health screen checks that chat can connect by making one request from your site to its own REST API address (a “loopback” request). It is sent to your own domain and nothing is sent anywhere else.
  • Team members’ pictures in the Inbox come from WordPress’s own avatar setting, which uses Gravatar by default. You can change or switch this off under Settings → Discussion. The plugin itself sends nothing to Gravatar.
